language_uris.description: Language URIs from EU Authority Table

spatial_uris.description: Spatial coverage URIs (e.g. EU NUTS codes)

accrual_periodicity.description: Update frequency URI from MDR frequency table

conforms_to.description: URI of a standard or specification the dataset conforms to

ontologyConfig.description: Semantic model binding: which mapping spec says what this dataset's columns mean. dataset-api derives GET /catalogue/{id}/vocabulary from it. Distinct from dcat.conforms_to, which names the model itself rather than the mapping onto these columns — several datasets can conform to one model through different mappings.

spec.description: Name of a SHARED mapping spec published in celine-ontologies (e.g. 'obs_rec_energy') — no path, no extension. Use this when the dataset has the same shape as others; meter readings and forecasts recur across producers and the mapping should not be restated per dataset.

spec_file.description: Path to a mapping spec file, relative to the directory holding this governance.yaml (e.g. './mappings/rec_custom.yaml'). Use this when the dataset's shape is its own. Keeping it beside the pipeline matters because a spec names SOURCE COLUMNS, and those columns are what the pipeline emits — a spec in another repository goes stale on a rename with nothing to detect it.

dataspaceConfig.description: Dataspace exposure and ODRL policy hints

expose.description: Expose this dataset in the EDC dataspace catalogue

contract_required.description: Require a signed contract before data access

odrl_action.description: Primary ODRL action granted (use, distribute, reproduce)

dependency.description: One dataset this pipeline consumes. Names a DATASET, never a pipeline: several producers may satisfy one dataset through a shared alias (the weather__* contract tables), and a deployment may substitute its own producer. The producing pipeline is resolved by matching this pattern against the `sources` keys of every governance file in the scanned set, so nothing here ever names a repository.

dataset.description: Dataset name in the same vocabulary as a `sources` key — `<database>.<schema>.<table>`, literal or fnmatch glob. Prefer a glob over the schema segment: `ds_dev_*` is the platform default and stays the default everywhere, since environments are separated by infrastructure rather than by renaming schemas, but a consumer resolves the schema through CELINE_SILVER_SCHEMA / CELINE_GOLD_SCHEMA and a deployment may point those anywhere. `datasets.*_gold.pv_overture_buildings` is the form that does not depend on that choice.

external.description: No pipeline in this set produces it; it is satisfied elsewhere. States the author's expectation, so that an entry which resolves to nothing AND is not marked external can be reported as a typo rather than being indistinguishable from a genuine external upstream. Never name the producing repository — the role is the identification.

optional.description: A soft edge: run after the producer when it exists, but do not require it. For a consumer that degrades rather than fails, as pv_estimation does when pv_detection has not run.

expose.description: Listed in the catalogue and served by the API: gates /catalogue* and /query. Omit to inherit dataspace.expose, which is how every file written before this field behaves and why adding it changes nothing until a file states it. Combined with dataspace.expose as AND — offering a dataset that is not listed is a contradiction, since a consumer reaches a dataspace asset through its catalogue entry, and the exporter rejects it rather than resolving it silently.

attribution.description: Required attribution text for dataset usage and redistribution

access_level.description: open=public, internal=org only, restricted=contract+consent, secret=omit from catalogue

access_requirements.description: Preconditions required to access this dataset

handler.description: Row filter handler name (e.g. rec_registry, direct_user_match, http_in_list)

row_filters.description: Row filter specs for row-level access control. Each entry selects a handler and its args.

defaults.description: Default governance applied to all datasets unless overridden

active.description: Whether this pipeline is on a schedule anywhere. `false` covers both retired (superseded by another pipeline) and local-only (run on demand against a local database); the two are not distinguished because for the graph they are the same statement — its datasets stay catalogued, but nothing new arrives unless someone acts. App-level, and that is a real limit: one app can host several flows on independent schedules and a deployment can pause one of them, which this cannot express. Per-flow state lives in the deployment, which is the only thing that knows it.

depends_on.description: Datasets this pipeline CONSUMES, as `sources` names what it produces. Optional, and absent is not the same as empty: absent means the pipeline has not declared its inputs, `[]` means it declares that it has none. A pipeline with no upstream in this repository omits it.

sources.description: Map of dataset name patterns → governance rules (exact match or fnmatch glob)
